card.statement:
(Quantum Hikita conjecture).

Let $X,X^{!}$ be symplectically dual. Then there exist

•

a bijection of the roots $\Sigma_{eq,+}\cong\Sigma_{Kah,+}^{!}$ ,

•

a compatible isomorphism of the ring of differential operators $R_{eq}\cong R_{Kah}^{!}$ ,

•

and a compatible isomorphism of the $D$ -modules $M_{eq,reg}\cong M_{Kah,reg}^{!}$ taking $1\in\mathcal{A}_{0}^{0}$ to $1\in H^{0}(X^{!})$ ,

extending the isomorphisms from the Hikita–Nakajima conjecture.

The compatibility of the isomorphisms refer to the following. First, there is an identification of the equivariant roots and the Kahler roots of $X$ , $X^{!}$ respectively, inducing an isomorphism of monoids $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\Sigma_{eq,+}\cong\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\Sigma_{Kah,+}$ . Together with the isomorphism $\mathcal{A}_{0}^{2}\cong H^{2}_{T^{!}\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X^{!})$ depicted by the equivariant Hikita conjecture, we have an isomorphism of graded $k[\hbar]$ -algebras

(2.21)

$R_{eq}:=k[z^{\mu}:\mu\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\Sigma_{eq,+}]\otimes\mathrm{Sym}\mathcal{A}_{0}^{2}\cong k[z^{\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\Sigma_{Kah,+}]\otimes\mathrm{Sym}H^{2}_{T^{!}\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X^{!})=:R_{Kah}^{!}.$

After localization, this isomorphism implies the isomorphism of graded algebras

(2.22)

$R_{eq,reg}\cong R_{Kah,reg}^{!}.$

Lastly, we should have an isomorphism

$M_{eq,reg}:=\mathscr{B}(\mathcal{A})[(1-z^{\mu})^{-1}]\cong\Lambda\otimes H^{*}_{T^{!}\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X^{!})=:M_{Kah,reg}^{!}$

of graded $R_{eq,reg}\cong R_{Kah,reg}^{!}$ -modules.
card.label: Conjecture 2.34

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
